data.why: the repository ships full example data for 12 sessions (time series, gaze CSVs, ELAN .eaf files, RQA/cross-wavelet JSON, board path images) in assets/, loaded directly by config.json; only the raw videos are excluded and every other tab works without them

goals: select a parent-child dyad session and a timeline point, then compare ball-trajectory kinematics against each partner's gaze on a shared time axis

inspect a recurrence (RQA) plot per kinematic signal to see when the ball returns to a prior state, and separately view each partner's categorical gaze RQA to see when their attention returns to a previously-viewed region
check cross-wavelet coherence between velocity components across time and timescale, judging a coherent region against a Monte Carlo chance level rather than visual thickness alone
read the ELAN annotation tiers aligned to the video/timeline to relate coded behavior to the kinematic and gaze signals
compare sessions with full exports against the two partially-built sessions (CUF00_L1_A1, CUF00_L1_A2) to see what degrades when gaze/ELAN/logged positions are missing

review.summary: The tree describes this multimodal parent–child dashboard accurately and honestly, and records where the interface falls short of its README (no gaze traces in the time series, no Monte Carlo chance level, an ELAN 404 for the partial sessions). Most cited screens show what their nodes claim. It needs a cleanup pass before filing: drop the display-settings phase, merge the zoom task, tighten a few over-claiming specific labels and session-selection citations, and add cross-session comparison and a time-series stack feature.
